content: 1. Discontinue the medication if adverse effects occur. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir decrease the levels or effects of omeprazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitor closely for reduced omeprazole efficacy and consider increasing the omeprazole dose if symptoms are not well controlled, but do not exceed 40 mg/day. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Clarithromycin and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended in patients with congenital long QT syndrome, electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure, or bradyarrhythmias. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Clarithromycin and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 8. Clarithromycin and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole increases the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 10. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Monitor closely. 11. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Clarithromycin and oxaliplatin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Oxcarbazepine increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor closely. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. A dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Clarithromycin and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. Monitor closely. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel protein-bound by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Monitor closely. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Clarithromycin and paliperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat is known to significantly prolong the QT interval, and its prescribing information states that use with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. Monitor closely. 24. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Clarithromycin and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration of pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH. Consider using short-acting antacids instead of PPIs and H2 antagonists, and separate antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose according to the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 32. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of penicillin G aqueous and penicillin VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 33. Clarithromycin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 34. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor closely. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Clarithromycin and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose according to the drug monograph. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration of PPIs with pexidartinib. Use H2-receptor antagonists or antacids if needed, and administer pexidartinib two hours before or after taking locally-acting antacids, or at least two hours before or ten hours after taking an H2-receptor antagonist. 38. Clarithromycin increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor closely. 40. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole and clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor closely. 41. Omeprazole decreases the levels of phytoestrogens by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin and pimavanserin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Clarithromycin and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels of pimozide by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current pirtobrutinib dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Once the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for five half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the dose taken before initiating the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 47. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 48. Clarithromycin and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration of polatuzumab vedotin with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase unconjugated MMAE AUC, potentially increasing polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Clarithromycin increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Omeprazole decreases the levels of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, decrease the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. 53. Clarithromycin and ponesimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Clarithromycin and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 55. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Clarithromycin increases the levels of pravastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for myopathy and do not exceed a pravastatin dose of 40 mg/day when co-administered.
